subject.title: [Bug]: Subagent completion silently lost — no retry, no notification, no auto-restart on timeout

question: Should subagent completion failures be solved by a durable completion outbox/recovery contract, or should maintainers first accept a narrower retry-and-notification mitigation?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans retry timing, duplicate prevention, session wake/consume semantics, restart/orphan recovery, task ledger state, and channel-visible failure policy, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Design durable delivery first
options.body: Use this issue and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777 to settle payload persistence, retry, failure visibility, and duplicate-prevention before landing another partial fix.

options.title: Ship a narrow mitigation
options.body: Allow https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90561 or a replacement only after merge blockers are fixed and live requester-visible proof shows the intended signal without duplicates.

options.title: Split narrower modes
options.body: Keep this broad issue as the umbrella while routing active-run consumption, timeout/restart, and channel-specific variants to focused linked issues.

recommendation.title: Design durable delivery first
recommendation.body: Use this issue and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777 to settle payload persistence, retry, failure visibility, and duplicate-prevention before landing another partial fix.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for the registry lifecycle/helpers boundary where the durable delivery decision would land.
